state.title: fix(ci): raise cmd-gc-productmetrics-testhook's timeout to fit the runner it actually gets
state.body:
## Summary
- Fixes #6396: `cmd-gc-productmetrics-testhook`'s `timeout-minutes: 5` was budgeting compile time, not test time -- its own timing artifact shows six tests taking 0.87s total against a 4m37 job on main, because `runner-policy` resolves `runner_32vcpu` to plain `ubuntu-latest` (4 vCPU) for every non-maintainer login, and any `go.sum` change colds the `actions/setup-go` cache and pushes the job over budget -- a hard cancellation with no failing test in the log.
- The issue proposed two fixes: (1) give the job a warm build cache, or (2) size the timeout for the runner it actually gets. Went with (2) only -- `.github/actions/setup-gascity-ubuntu` doesn't configure anything Go-cache-specific beyond what `actions/setup-go` already does inline in this job (both call the identical pinned `actions/setup-go` action); the "warm cache" effect the issue observed looks more like cache-population timing across jobs in the same workflow run, which isn't verifiable or safely restructurable without live GitHub Actions runner behavior to test against.
- Raised `timeout-minutes` to 12 -- safe, minimal, directly fixes the reported false-cancellation, and is explicitly endorsed by the issue itself as a valid stopgap.

## Test plan
- Not a Go change -- validated the YAML parses and confirmed no other docs reference the old 5-minute figure.
